about: Customer support replies for a made-up online shop, with planted failures and a written answer key.
reference:
# Sofa So Good: customer support policy

Sofa So Good is a fictional online shop that sells kitchenware, lamps and home textiles. This policy is made up for testing and describes no real company.

## Returns
- Items can be returned within **30 days of delivery** if unused and in their original packaging.
- Refunds go back to the original payment method within **5-7 business days** after the return arrives at our warehouse.
- **Clearance items are final sale** and can't be returned or exchanged, unless they arrive damaged or defective.
- Return shipping is **free when the item is damaged, defective or not what was ordered**. For any other return, a **$6.95** prepaid label is deducted from the refund.

## Damaged or defective items
- Customers should report damage or defects **within 14 days of delivery**, with a photo.
- We send a replacement or a refund, whichever the customer prefers.
- For damaged items **under $25**, the customer keeps or recycles the item; no return is needed.

## Shipping
- Standard shipping takes **3-7 business days**. Express takes **1-2 business days**.
- Agents may give these estimates, but **must never guarantee a delivery date**.

## Order changes
- Orders can be cancelled or changed (address, items) **within 1 hour** of being placed. After that, the order ships as placed, and the customer can return it once it arrives.

## Price adjustments
- If an item's price drops **within 7 days of purchase**, we refund the difference **once per item**. Clearance items aren't eligible.

## Goodwill
- If a delivery is more than **5 business days later than its estimate**, agents may offer a **one-time 10% discount code** for a future order.
- Agents may not offer any other discount, credit, free item or fee waiver.

## Warranty
- Electrical items (kettles, toasters, lamps) carry a **1-year warranty** against manufacturing defects from the date of delivery.

## When to escalate
Agents must hand these to a specialist and must not try to resolve them alone. The reply acknowledges the issue, says a specialist will reply **within 1 business day**, and gives any immediate safety advice.
- An injury or safety hazard: burns, fire, smoke, sparks, electric shock.
- Legal action: the customer mentions a lawyer, a lawsuit, or a complaint to a regulator.
- A chargeback or payment dispute with the customer's bank.
- Suspected fraud or account compromise: orders the customer didn't place, or a changed password or email they didn't change.
- A lost order worth more than **$500**.
- A customer who has asked for a manager **twice** in the conversation.

## Tone and privacy
- Be polite, plain and specific. Don't blame the customer.
- Never ask for a full card number or a password.

good.name: Accurate to policy
good.pass: Everything the reply states or promises (rules, time frames, prices, discounts, warranty, what happens next) matches the reference policy and the facts in the customer's message. Judge only what the reply says: something left out is judged by 'Answers the question', and whether the case should go to a specialist is judged by 'Escalates when required'. So a reply that deals with a case itself when it should have gone to a specialist doesn't fail here for that reason.
fail_examples: States a wrong return window, fee or deadline
Offers a discount, credit or free item the policy doesn't allow
Says something is allowed that the policy forbids

good.name: Answers the question
good.pass: The reply directly addresses everything the customer asked, or, when it can't answer yet, says clearly what will happen next and when. Judge only whether each question is addressed: whether the answer is correct is judged by 'Accurate to policy', and whether the case should go to a specialist by 'Escalates when required'.
fail_examples: Answers only one of two questions
Gives generic text with no answer and no next step

good.name: Escalates when required
good.pass: When the message matches one of the policy's escalation triggers, the reply hands the case to a specialist, says they will reply within 1 business day, and gives immediate safety advice where relevant. When no trigger applies, the reply handles the request itself.
fail_examples: An injury, fire, smoke or sparks is handled as a normal return
A lawyer, chargeback or fraud is mentioned and the reply tries to resolve it alone
A second request for a manager is ignored

good.name: Appropriate tone
good.pass: Polite, plain and respectful. No blame, sarcasm, condescension or shouting.
fail_examples: Curt to the point of dismissive
Tells the customer to read the FAQ before contacting support

vague.name: Handles the situation
vague.pass: The reply handles the situation appropriately.

rows.input: Hi, my order SSG-48216 arrived five days ago, and I finally had a chance to unpack everything this morning. I’m sorry that two plates in your dinnerware set arrived chipped, especially when you were looking forward to using it in your new dining room. Thank you for sending photos of both plates. Since your order was delivered five days ago, you’ve reported the damage within our 14-day reporting window.

Because the set cost $220, the no-return option that applies to damaged items under $25 does not automatically apply here.

As for your toaster, it has a one-year warranty against manufacturing defects, measured from its date of delivery. That warranty is separate from the issue with the dinnerware. Thank you for giving us the opportunity to help with both questions.

Maya
